intro: Around 500 BCE, China was breaking apart. The Zhou kings had lost their power, and rival states fought for land and survival. Rulers wanted advice, and thinkers traveled from court to court to give it. This troubled age produced some of the most important philosophy in world history.

In this unit you will meet the Zhou and their Mandate of Heaven, Confucius on the road, and the Hundred Schools of Thought. You will read Mozi on caring for all and Han Feizi on reward and punishment. You will follow Qin's rise, the burning of the books, and the Han choice of Confucian learning.

By the end, you will be able to place the thinkers on a timeline and compare what each school taught. You will be able to tell a primary source from a later legend. And you will be able to explain how historians weigh a story like the burning of the books.
bigQuestion: How did war and rivalry among states shape the ideas that became the Chinese classics?

timeline.t: The Zhou overthrow the Shang and claim the Mandate of Heaven
The Zhou court moves east; the Spring and Autumn period begins
Confucius is born in Lu (traditional date; died 479 BCE)
Shang Yang begins Legalist reforms in Qin
Qin unifies China; its king becomes the First Emperor
Qin orders many books burned, as Sima Qian reports
Qin falls; the Han dynasty begins
The Han found the Imperial Academy to teach the classics
Sima Qian finishes the Shiji, with lives of Confucius and Laozi

words.d: a line of rulers from the same family
the idea that Heaven gives the right to rule to the virtuous and can take it away
475–221 BCE, when seven large states fought until Qin united China
the many schools of philosophy in China before 221 BCE
evidence from the time being studied
a story passed down about a person or event that cannot be proven
acting without forcing; a key Daoist idea
impartial care for all; Mozi's teaching
the school of strict law, reward and punishment, linked to Han Feizi
a government controlling or banning what people can read or say
the Han school, founded 124 BCE, that trained officials in the classics

test.q: What did the Mandate of Heaven allow the Zhou to claim?
test.why: The Zhou said Heaven had given them the mandate to rule after the Shang.

test.q: What happened to Zhou kings after 771 BCE?
choices: They lost real power to the states
test.why: After the move east, the Zhou kings held title and rites but little power.

test.q: Why did Confucius travel for years?
choices: To find a ruler who would use his ideas
test.why: He sought a ruler who would put his teaching into practice.

test.q: Which is a later legend about Confucius?
choices: A qilin appeared at his birth
His sayings are in the Analects
test.why: The qilin story is legend; the others rest on early sources.

test.q: Which Daoist idea means acting without forcing?
test.why: Wu wei is the Daoist idea of acting without forcing.

test.q: Who taught jian ai, impartial care?
test.why: Mozi taught impartial care and opposed aggressive war.

test.q: In the Mozi's Gongshu story, what did Mozi do?
test.why: Mozi walked to Chu and defended against Gongshu Ban's model attacks, stopping the war.

test.q: What did Han Feizi call reward and punishment?
test.why: Han Feizi called them the ruler's two handles.

test.q: Which thinker compared rulers who copy ancient kings to a farmer waiting by a stump?
test.why: The stump story is in the Han Feizi, ch. 49.
Qin completed its conquest in 221 BCE.

test.q: Which books did Qin spare from burning?
test.why: Sima Qian reports that practical books were spared.

test.q: Why do some historians question parts of the Qin story?
choices: Han writers had reasons to paint Qin badly
Sima Qian was a Qin minister
test.why: Sima Qian and other Han writers served the dynasty that replaced Qin.

test.q: Under which ruler did Confucian learning become official?
test.why: Emperor Wu of Han gave Confucian learning official status.

test.q: What does Analects 2.3 prefer to rule by punishment?
test.why: Confucius says leading by virtue and propriety gives people a sense of shame and makes them good.

write.prompt: Which is the better way to keep order: virtue and ritual, or clear laws with reward and punishment? Do not choose; instead, explain both sides. Cite Analects 2.3 (Legge, 1893) and Han Feizi's 'two handles' or stump story (paraphrased), and describe how later readers weighed Qin.
tips: Name each text and its chapter, like Analects 2.3 or Han Feizi ch. 49.
Attribute each view: "Confucius taught..." or "Han Feizi argued..."
Compare the schools rather than judging them.
Use unit words such as ren, Legalism and Mandate of Heaven.
